binders: Real-valued random variables X1,...,XN on a common probability space.
An arbitrary real coefficient vector a=(a1,...,aN) in R^N.
A real threshold t with t>=0.
A positive absolute constant c, uniform over N, the probability space, the family, a, and t.
hypotheses: The random variables X1,...,XN are mutually independent.
conclusions: For every t>=0, P{|sum_{i=1}^N a_i X_i|>=t} <= 2 exp[-c min(t^2/(K^2 ||a||_2^2), t/(K ||a||_infinity))], where K=max_{1<=i<=N} ||X_i||_psi1.
definitions_and_conventions: The weighted random sum is S_a=sum_{i=1}^N a_i X_i.
||a||_2 is the Euclidean norm of the coefficient vector.
The event is two-sided because it uses |S_a|>=t.
The symbol ||X_i||_psi1 denotes the established sub-exponential norm.
implicit_context: N is nonzero because the source lists X1,...,XN, uses R^N, and takes a maximum over the family.
All variables share one probability space so that their weighted sum and mutual independence are defined.
The constant c is inherited from the application of Theorem 2.8.1 and is absolute, hence independent of the theorem's data.
If K>0 and a!=0, then both displayed denominators are strictly positive and have their ordinary real meanings.
For a finite real vector, ||a||_2=0 and ||a||_infinity=0 are each equivalent to a=0.

details: There is a universal positive absolute constant c.
After the family and arbitrary coefficient vector are fixed, the inequality holds for every t>=0.
Each X_i is multiplied by the corresponding real coefficient a_i.
The absolute value makes the tail estimate two-sided.
The printed real quotients are unambiguously defined when K>0 and a!=0.
They are not given an interpretation when K=0 or a=0.

undebatable_constraints: The source family is finite and nonempty in its X1,...,XN convention.
The variables are independent, mean zero, and sub-exponential.
The coefficient vector a is arbitrary in R^N; the theorem does not assume a!=0.
The threshold range is every t>=0.
The exponent is -c times a minimum.
The quadratic term is exactly t^2/(K^2 ||a||_2^2).
The linear term is exactly t/(K ||a||_infinity).
K is exactly max_i ||X_i||_psi1, including indices whose coefficients may be zero.
The constant c is positive and absolute.
No separate zero-scale or zero-vector conclusion is printed.

contract_plain_english: There is a positive universal constant c such that, for any finite nonempty independent mean-zero sub-exponential family and any real coefficient vector a, the absolute weighted sum satisfies the two-regime Bernstein bound 2 exp[-c min(t^2/(K^2 ||a||_2^2), t/(K ||a||_infinity))] for every t>=0, where K is the largest component psi-one norm. The printed formula has unresolved effective-domain defects when K=0 or a=0 because both rate denominators then vanish, including 0/0 at t=0, and the source gives neither positivity hypotheses nor explicit degenerate branches.
